titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 4/2007 (އޮޑިޓް ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ...... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Audit Act (Law No. 4/2007) by adding a new paragraph, 9(ha-1), to Article 9. It gives the Auditor General the power to require members of independent commissions, holders of independent posts, and heads of statutory bodies, offices and agencies to submit statements of their assets and money, to receive those statements, and to publish them. Each official would have to file a statement of their holdings within 30 days of taking office, and a yearly statement checked by a licensed auditor within 90 days after each year in office ends. Anyone who breaks these requirements could be fined MVR 5,000. The explanatory note lists 26 posts and bodies it has in mind, from the Elections Commission to the Commissioner of Police.
whyItMatters: If passed, the asset and money declarations of senior officials in independent and statutory bodies would be collected by the Auditor General and made public, so anyone could look them up.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 adds paragraph (ha-1) after paragraph (ha) of Article 9, letting the Auditor General ask the covered officials for statements of their assets and money, receive them and publish them.

Sub-paragraph (1): a yearly statement verified by an auditor licensed by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of the Maldives, due within 90 days after the end of each year counted from the date the official took office.
Sub-paragraph (2): on taking office, a statement of the official's assets, money, business interests and debts as of the day they took the oath, due within 30 days.
Sub-paragraph (3): anyone who breaks the requirements can be fined MVR 5,000 (the text refers to numbers (1) and (3), which appears to mean (1) and (2)).
Clause 2: the law takes effect once it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Members of constitutional commissions and tribunals and the heads of authorities and agencies such as the Prosecutor General, Commissioner of Police and Commissioner General of Taxation, plus the Auditor General's office, which would collect and publish their statements.
statedReasons: The note says there is no clear system for these officials to declare and disclose their assets and money, and the rules sit across the Constitution and many laws, so the bill puts one requirement in a single law instead of amending all of them.
